prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK Manifesto 2024 (policy measures only)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; stop small boat crossings via detention, offshore processing, and returns; create a Department of Immigration.
- Target zero NHS waiting lists while keeping services free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; scrap energy levies and Net Zero; expand domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential visas; ban asylum from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens; secure detention and rapid processing; immediate deportation after sentences for foreign offenders; withdraw citizenship for serious crimes.
- Restrict international students’ dependents; close abusive courses; five-year residency and employment for benefit eligibility.
- Employer Immigration Tax: raise employer NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care and micro-firms).
- Estimated savings £5–10bn pa; employer tax ~£4bn pa.

Government spending and regulation
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves (~£35bn pa saving).
- 5% efficiency saving across departments without cutting frontlines (~£50bn pa).
- Cut foreign aid by 50% (~£6bn pa); reduce EU-derived and other regulations; improve HMRC tax collection.

Personal taxation and cost of living
- Income tax threshold to £20k; higher rate from £70k.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy; scrap environmental levies.
- Stamp Duty: 0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% above.
- Reinstate VAT-free shopping for tourists.
- Inheritance Tax: 0% under £2m; 20% above (charity option).
- Cost ~£70bn pa.

Business
- No Corporation Tax for profits under £100k; main rate to 20%, then 15% in year 3.
- Abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning reform; significant deregulation including employment rules; tax simplification.
- Cost ~£18bn pa.

NHS
- Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS/social care staff for 3 years; expand UK medical training; write off fees over 10 years’ service.
- Use independent capacity domestically and abroad; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if GP wait >3 days, consultant >3 weeks, operation >9 weeks; weekend theatres; charge for no-shows; “Pharmacy First.”
- Cost ~£17bn pa.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and related subsidies; remove ~£10bn pa renewable subsidies via equivalent taxation.
- Fast-track North Sea oil/gas; shale test sites; SMRs and other technologies.
- Estimated savings ~£30bn pa.

Law, order, and justice
- Recruit 40,000 police over 5 years; expand stop and search; tougher sentencing for violent and drug offences; new leadership standards; phase out PCSOs; remove DEI roles.
- Justice: automatic life for violent repeat offenders; budget from £10bn to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; redefine hate crime; 10,000 new prison places.
- Policing cost ~£3bn pa; justice cost ~£2bn pa.

Education
- Revise curriculum; restrict gender-related interventions in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; limit undergraduate numbers; enforce entry standards.
- Strengthen free speech enforcement; expand Pupil Referral Units; offer 2-year degrees.
- Cost ~£5bn pa.

Welfare
- Tighten assessments; two-strike rule for job offers; incentives for apprenticeships and return to work. Savings ~£15bn pa.

Brexit and constitutional
- Repeal retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA.
- Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act; reform House of Lords and Civil Service leadership; restrict postal voting; consider PR via referendum; British Bill of Rights. Largely cost-neutral.

Defence and veterans
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay uplift; Armed Forces Justice Bill; create a Veterans Department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform; free education during/after service. Cost ~£14bn pa.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield; prioritize locals in social housing; reverse Section 24 for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections. Cost-neutral.

Families and children
- Transferable marriage allowance (25%) when affordable; front-load child benefit ages 1–4; single-sex facilities; assess social media harms. Cost ~£8bn pa.

Transport and infrastructure
- Scrap HS2 (save ~£25bn one-off); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; no phase-out of petrol/diesel mandates; accelerate regional upgrades.
- New 50/50 public–pension fund ownership model for utilities; cap standing charges; streamline infrastructure funding. Savings ~£5bn pa (first 5 years).

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked subsidies with direct payments; reduce red tape; “Buy British” targets; CMA powers on pricing. Cost ~£2bn pa.
- Fishing: end automatic EU access; paid licences; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing; training and fleet growth. Cost ~£2bn pa.

Pensions and social care
- Royal Commission on social care; clamp down on offshore tax practices; pension system review; amend Mineworkers’ Pension Scheme.

Funding summary (per manifesto)
- Potential savings ~£150bn pa + £10bn pa from assumed extra growth; total ~£160bn pa.
- Total costs ~£141bn pa.
